reasoning: The core PROBLEM — that "diverse" LLM panels lose most of their nominal independence because models make the same mistakes on the same items — is already firmly established. "Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes" (arXiv 2605.29800) computes exactly the correlated-error / effective-votes statistic the proposal wants (panel of 9 LLMs from 7 families provides ~2 independent votes), and Kim et al. "Correlated Errors in LLMs" (ICML 2025, arXiv 2506.07962) gives a large-scale empirical demonstration that LLM errors are correlated and worse for accurate/same-family models, with downstream impact on LLM-as-judge. The LessWrong "Ensemble monitoring for AI control" post measures pairwise correlation of monitor suspicion scores on attack samples directly in the safety-monitoring setting. What remains genuinely unexplored is the precise framing: a clean cross-family panel of open-weight models run as YES/NO harmfulness monitors over a public safety dataset, reporting the correlated-MISS rate on unsafe items versus the independence product specifically (the judge/NLI papers are not safety-monitoring, and the AI-control post uses mostly one base model and frames it as ensemble-building, listing "which attacks each monitor uniquely catches" as future work). So the underlying claim is largely known, but this specific safety-monitor miss-correlation measurement is a modest, replication-flavored gap.

evidence.title: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels
evidence.summary: Panel of 9 frontier LLMs from 7 families provides only ~2 independent votes' worth of information; ~3/4 of nominal independence lost because models err on the same items. Computes the exact effective-votes/correlated-error statistic the proposal wants, but on NLI/evaluation tasks, not safety/harmfulness monitoring.

evidence.title: Correlated Errors in Large Language Models (Kim, Garg, Peng, Garg)
evidence.summary: Large-scale empirical study (350+ LLMs) showing model errors are substantially correlated, more so for accurate models and same developer/architecture, with downstream effects on LLM-as-judge and hiring. Establishes the problem-level finding but is not framed around safety monitors missing unsafe outputs.

evidence.title: Ensemble monitoring for AI control: diverse signals outweigh...
evidence.summary: Directly in the safety-monitoring/AI-control setting: builds 12 monitors and quantifies diversity as inverse of average pairwise correlation in suspicion scores on attack samples; finds diverse monitors have different biases. Uses mostly variants of one base model and frames it as how to build better ensembles; explicitly lists 'which attacks each monitor uniquely catches' as future work.

evidence.title: AutoMonitor-Bench: Evaluating the Reliability of LLM-Based Misbehavior Monitors
evidence.summary: Evaluates 12 proprietary and 10 open-source LLMs as misbehavior monitors, finding substantial variability and a consistent miss-rate/false-alarm trade-off. Establishes per-monitor miss rates but does not center on correlation of misses across a panel / defense-in-depth independence.

evidence.title: SoK: Evaluating Jailbreak Guardrails for Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Systematization showing different guardrails catch different abnormal patterns and motivating ensemble/combination approaches (e.g., EGUARD); relevant adjacent context on guardrail complementarity but does not measure correlated-miss statistics across a diverse monitor panel.
